title: Automated proration-drift detector and corrective export for billing reconciler
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see small, persistent invoice mismatches between Redwood's usage ledger and downstream exports (Stripe/NetSuite). Root causes observed in incidents: late-arriving hourly usage, rate-limit/burst credit application timing, reserved-capacity discounts applied post-export, and DST/anchor-window edge cases. These drifts are often sub-dollar per invoice but accumulate and trigger customer disputes or accounting adjustments.

Goal: Build an automated detector that scans exports and the canonical usage ledger to identify proration/drift exceeding configurable thresholds, produce an auditable corrective delta, and append idempotent adjustment lines to the downstream export pipeline (or surface for manual review when above safety limits). The detector must: (1) operate on hourly and daily aggregation windows, (2) tolerate late arrivals with backfill windows, (3) generate correction metadata (idempotency key, reason, original invoice refs), and (4) integrate with the existing NetSuite/Stripe export flow with full traceability in the Console.

Non-goals: We will not rework billing math or pricing plans in this ticket. Large customer-facing credit reversals (> $50 or > 5% of invoice) will be flagged for manual ops review rather than auto-corrected in this rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Detector flags ledger vs export delta when abs(delta) > $0.50 OR percentage delta > 1% for any invoice window
Corrective export lines are generated with idempotency keys and a human-readable memo field and accepted by Stripe import sandbox and NetSuite staging import
Auto-corrections only apply when abs(delta) <= $5 AND customer_impact = none/low; larger deltas create a ticket for Finance/Ops
End-to-end integration test that simulates late usage arrival and rate-limit credits results in either a corrective export line or a manual task as per the rulebook
Dashboard shows daily counts of detected drifts, total dollar corrections, and mean time to reconcile; alerts fire when daily corrections > $2000
Export has audit trail linking adjustment back to the canonical usage rows and the reconciler job run ID
implementation_notes: Add nightly reconciler job: billing.reconciler.proration_drift_detector (kicked in staging -> canary -> prod)
Join canonical hourly_usage_ledger to hourly_export_snapshot by invoice_window and customer_id; compute signed delta and percent_delta
Backfill policy: include late-arriving usage within 72 hours for hourly windows; mark any change affecting a previously exported invoice as "correctable" per thresholds
Generate adjustment payloads: Stripe invoice item with description 'Proration correction: reconciler-run-{run_id}'; NetSuite CSV/GL line with memo containing reconciler metadata
Idempotency: use deterministic id format 'recon|{customer_id}|{invoice_window}|{checksum}' and persist in reconciler_adjustments table
Safety: auto-apply only when abs(delta) <= $5 and not impacting reserved-capacity discount breakdowns; if reserved-capacity fields differ, create manual review ticket
Observability: emit metrics (drift_count, drift_amount_usd, corrected_count, corrected_amount_usd, manual_review_count) to metrics pipeline and add Grafana dashboard
Testing: create unit tests for delta computation, integration tests for Stripe/NetSuite sandbox import, load test job with synthetic late usage arrival patterns
runbook_summary: If the reconciler auto-applies an adjustment, the export will include memo 'proration-reconciler' and a link to the reconciler UI. Finance should verify during next billing run. For manual-review items, the job will open a ticket to billing-ops with prefilled reconciliation details. To revert an erroneous auto-apply, Finance Ops can issue a reversing invoice item using the reconciler's reversal helper endpoint (requires approval).
comments: 2025-11-03 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after Q4 customer dispute spike; initial investigation shows many small deltas caused by late rate-limit credits and DST anchor-window mismatches.

2025-11-10 - Miguel Fernandez: Spike repro in staging. Built prototype SQL to compute per-invoice delta and validate idempotency key scheme. Prototype attached: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-reconciler/pull/213

2025-12-02 - Finance review (Lina Cho): Agreed on safety thresholds: auto-correct up to $5 and <=1% of invoice. Anything larger should create manual ticket to Ops with suggested customer communication text.

2026-01-18 - Design review (Ben O'Connor): Console should surface corrections with a compact table: run_id, customer, invoice_window, delta_usd, action(taken/manual), link to export row. Prototype UI in Figma: https://drive.google.com/figma/proration-reconciler-ui
2026-02-05 - Eng notes: Implemented reconciler job and adjustment persistence table. Running daily in staging; observed ~120 detects/day, ~95% below $5 threshold. Shipping to canary next week.

2026-03-01 - QA (Priya Raman): Integration test failures with NetSuite staging import due to CSV column order. Adjusted exporter to conform to NetSuite mapping v2 and added acceptance test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-reconciler/pull/287
2026-03-10 - SRE (Evan Li): Added alert when daily corrected_amount_usd > 2000 and when reconciler job runtime > 30m. Also instrumented job with trace IDs for easier postmortems.

2026-03-14 - Miguel Fernandez: Canary rollout successful for 10% of customers. Observability dashboard: mean correction = $0.92, median = $0.12. Proceeding with 100% rollout on 2026-03-21 pending final Finance signoff.
